acceptance_criteria.criterion: ComputeAsync on an obfuscated-extension path returns the filename stem (uppercase) and makes zero calls to IFfprobeRunner.
ComputeAsync on the same native-extension input produces identical output across two calls (determinism).
When the ffprobe JSON contains a duplicate key, only the first occurrence is captured.
A JSON numeric literal 1.0 is stored as the string "1.0", not "1" (raw token text semantics).
Keys absent from the ffprobe JSON are silently omitted from the join (no empty placeholder).

Selected 41 keys in spec-defined order, joined with '|', ASCII-encoded, MD5.HashData, returned as Convert.ToHexString (uppercase).

comments.note: PathBasedVideoHasher.cs: plan.md §Hashing pipeline says ValueSpan should be 'decoded as ASCII' for number tokens, but implementation uses Encoding.UTF8.GetString(reader.ValueSpan). Functionally equivalent since JSON number tokens are pure ASCII characters (digits, '.', 'e', 'E', '+', '-'). Not a bug, but a minor deviation from the plan's wording.

Files with no extension: Path.GetExtension returns empty string, TrimStart('.') = empty string, IsObfuscated('') returns false — correctly falls through to ffprobe. No test covers this explicit path but the code handles it correctly by design.

AC-1 test covers 4 of 9 unique obfuscated extensions (.raz, .dic, .pkg, .dat). Remaining 5 (.res, .stf, .llz, .wwd, .vkg) share identical code paths via IsObfuscated(); gap is acceptable but noted for completeness.

summary: Reviewed 2 files: PathBasedVideoHasher.cs and PathBasedVideoHasherTests.cs. All 10 OWASP categories assessed. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 1 Low (ASCII silent replacement collision), 1 Info (MD5 as content identifier — spec-mandated). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A02/A04 — ASCII Encoding Silent Replacement (PathBasedVideoHasher.cs, line ~82): Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes(concatenated) silently maps non-ASCII characters to '?' (0x3F). Two files whose ffprobe metadata differs only in non-ASCII characters (e.g., 'Café' vs 'Caf€') will produce identical hashes. This is a spec-mandated behavior (hashing-specification.md §5) and is not attacker-controlled in the current architecture. Recommendation: document this known collision vector in the class summary and ensure callers in the indexing pipeline are aware that library deduplication may incorrectly merge files with non-ASCII-only metadata differences.

A04 — Input Validation (PathBasedVideoHasher.cs, ComputeHashAsync): filePath is only null-checked (ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull). No validation against path traversal sequences ('..'), UNC paths ('\\server\share'), or excessive length. The class delegates to IFfprobeRunner which may spawn an external process. If callers ever expose filePath derivation to user input, this becomes a path traversal risk. Recommendation: document the trust boundary assumption that filePath has already been validated by the caller (library management layer), or add a Path.IsPathRooted/Path.GetFullPath normalisation guard at this layer for defence-in-depth.

A02 — MD5 as Content Identifier (PathBasedVideoHasher.cs, line ~85): MD5 is a cryptographically broken hash function susceptible to intentional collisions. In this role as a content fingerprint/deduplication key (not as a security or integrity hash), the collision risk is negligible for unintentional matches on real media metadata. However, a determined attacker who can craft metadata values could engineer a collision to cause false deduplication. This risk is accepted per spec §5 and QA handoff notes. Recommendation: retain as Info — no remediation required unless the hash is ever repurposed for integrity or security verification.

A03 — Injection Surface Note (PathBasedVideoHasher.cs, ComputeHashAsync): filePath is forwarded directly to IFfprobeRunner.ProbeAsync without sanitisation. PathBasedVideoHasher itself performs no shell execution, so there is no injection risk in this class. The injection surface (if any) lives in FfprobeRunner. This note is provided for completeness; the FfprobeRunner implementation should be audited when its WP is processed to confirm argument passing is safe (e.g., uses Process.Start with ArgumentList rather than shell-concatenated strings).

One Fix-Forward applied: class-level <remarks> used <paramref name="obfuscationMap"/> to reference a method parameter in a type-level doc comment — replaced with <see cref="IObfuscationMap"/> which is the correct XML doc tag for cross-referencing a type at the class level.

comments.note: PathBasedVideoHasher.cs, class-level <remarks>: Replaced `<paramref name="obfuscationMap"/>` with `<see cref="IObfuscationMap"/>`. Using <paramref> at the type level to reference a method parameter produces a dangling reference in XML documentation tooling — the tag has no semantic target in that context. The correct tag for referencing a type is <see cref="..."/>. Non-behavioral doc correction.

[documentation-forward] PathBasedVideoHasher.cs, class-level <remarks>: Document the filePath trust boundary assumption — callers are expected to supply a pre-validated path (no path traversal sequences, no UNC paths). The Security Auditor flagged this (low risk, defence-in-depth). A <remarks> paragraph stating this assumption would make the class safe to use without readers needing to consult the audit trail.

[documentation-forward] PathBasedVideoHasher.cs, class-level <remarks>: The known ASCII-encoding collision vector (non-ASCII metadata values silently mapped to '?' by Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes, per spec §5) is documented only in the security audit pipeline. A brief note in the class-level XML doc would surface this known limitation to callers at the point of use.

PathBasedVideoHasherTests.cs: The ComputeExpectedMd5 test helper replicates Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes + MD5.HashData from the SUT. This means if the encoding were ever changed, the helper would also need updating and tests would still pass regardless. Not a bug, but reviewers should be aware the helper validates hash equality under the same encoding, not the encoding choice itself. Acceptable for current scope.

PathBasedVideoHasher.cs, ParseFlatDictionary: The default switch case correctly discards True/False/Null tokens per spec (only String/Integer captured). In practice ffprobe uses integers for boolean fields, so this is a non-issue. Worth noting if the spec is ever extended to cover boolean fields explicitly.

notes: PathBasedVideoHasher.cs is a new sealed class in VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Library. Key QA focus areas: (1) the obfuscated-extension early-exit path with various casing variants and all 10 known obfuscated extensions; (2) the Utf8JsonReader first-occurrence-wins semantics for duplicate keys at different nesting depths; (3) numeric literal raw-text preservation ('1.0' vs '1' vs '1.00'); (4) the full 41-key order matching the spec; (5) ASCII encoding of the final join string for the MD5 input.

PathBasedVideoHasher QA PASS. Key findings for Security Auditor: (1) MD5 is used intentionally as a content identifier (not a security/integrity hash) — this matches spec §5. Flag as informational only. (2) ASCII encoding of join string is spec-mandated — non-ASCII field values are silently mapped to '?' which could create hash collisions for files differing only in non-ASCII metadata chars; assess if this is an acceptable risk. (3) filePath parameter is not validated as a valid filesystem path — only null-checked. ProbeAsync receives it directly; security surface is in FfprobeRunner, not PathBasedVideoHasher. (4) No injection risk from filePath in this class since PathBasedVideoHasher never shells out directly.
